title: Self-balancing luminescence kinetics of charged excitons in WS$_2$ monolayer
authors: A. I. Veretennikov, A. I. Galimov, M. M. Glazov, T. V. Shubina
abstract: Two-dimensional tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenides exhibit a rich emission spectrum with distinct lines of exciton and biexciton states, neutral and charged, which are typically considered as independent entities. Here, we present a study of the emission kinetics of a WS$_2$ monolayer, demonstrating that these states together form a single interacting ensemble, with their population and depletion mutually coordinated with temperature. Dark trions make a long-lived contribution to the bright trion on a time scale of 200-300 picoseconds, and replenishment from dark states promotes intense luminescence of charged biexcitons. The developed self-consistent rate equation model reproduces the temperature dependence of the kinetics well, opening the way to controlling exciton states in such materials.
summary: This paper analyzes the complex photoluminescence kinetics in WS2 monolayers, showing that exciton emission arises from a single, interacting ensemble of charged and neutral states. By developing and applying a self-consistent rate equation model, the authors successfully reproduce the temperature dependence of the luminescence, revealing crucial roles for dark states in populating and sustaining the bright emission.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex, interacting luminescence kinetics of various charged and neutral exciton states within a WS2 monolayer.
main_result: The emission is not dominated by single-particle excitons but by an interacting ensemble, where dark trions contribute a long-lived component to the bright trion, and replenishment from dark states promotes intense charged biexciton luminescence.
method: The authors developed and utilized a self-consistent rate equation model, validated by time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) measurements across varying temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is a WS2 monolayer, modeled using rate equations that account for single-particle decay, temperature-dependent transitions (e.g., dark-to-bright), and nonlinear processes like biexciton formation.
key_observables: Characteristic decay times (fast, middle, slow components) for trions and biexcitons, and the temperature dependence of PL peak energies and intensities.
important_parameters: Temperature range (8 to 300 K), electron density ($\sim 10^{12} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$), and characteristic timescales (e.g., $200-300 	ext{ ps}$ for dark trion contribution).
main_assumptions: The model assumes that the population dynamics of all relevant exciton complexes can be described by coupled rate equations, and that the system is governed by thermal activation processes between states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the PL spectra decomposition, temperature dependence of peak energies/intensities, and the multi-component decay curves for the trion and biexciton lines.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and measurements (PL/TRPL) by reviewing prior work, develops a comprehensive rate equation model incorporating multiple interacting species, and then uses this model to fit and explain the temperature and time evolution of the observed luminescence kinetics.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed, quantitative framework for modeling open quantum systems in solid-state materials, specifically demonstrating how coupling between different quantum states (dark/bright excitons) dictates macroscopic optical properties.
